result.topic_en: Tables of residue classes for 22, 23, 26, 29 (and an unfinished 30) under + and − signs, apparently the linear forms of numbers of which ±a is a quadratic residue; below, written upside down, numerical calculations and a stated proposition about squares leaving the same remainder.

methods.what: Residue classes modulo 4a (or 2a) of numbers for which a = 22 has the stated character (sign +)
Residue classes for −22 as linear forms $88n\pm r$
Residue classes for ±23 (odd quadratic residues mod 23 as 46n+r; forms 92n±r)
Residue classes for ±26 as linear forms mod 104
Residue classes for ±29 as linear forms mod 116 and 58
Table of small primes with associated quadruples of numbers (apparently numbers whose squares give particular residues)

items.quote:
Propositio quae Demonstrationem exspectat
Si datur Quadratum, quod per $p$[?] divisum residuum $r$[?] efficit — dabitur idem Quadratum quod per
$4r+2$ divisum [-eandem-] det idem residuum; [-...-]
siquidem $4r+2$ sit numerus primus.
items.english: Proposition awaiting a demonstration: If there is a square which, divided by p, leaves remainder r, there will be the same square which, divided by 4r+2, gives the same remainder, provided 4r+2 is a prime number.
